meta.name: One-Person AI Company - Local Service Business
meta.description: Reference target architecture for a local service business run by one person with no employees. Five stages form a loop rather than a funnel: marketing rings the phone, intake catches it, sales books it, operations does the job, finance gets paid, and the collected cash sets next week's ad budget. Seven AI agent roles run it, and the approval gates sit on money and risk. Both are derived from the map by tools/ai_company.py rather than counted here, because a count in prose goes stale the first time a gate is added. Volumes are illustrative and sized for a one-van shop: 120 inbound leads a month, 96 real, 64 quoted, 38 won, average job around $1,450. Tool costs are deliberately absent - phase 1 of the readiness framework fills them from the business's real invoices, and a placeholder would be read as a fact. Replace every number here with the client's own before this becomes anyone's target design.

departments.name: Marketing & Demand
departments.description: Spends the budget that last week's collected cash decided. This is the stage that closes the loop: it is downstream of finance, not upstream of everything.

departments.name: Intake & Qualification
departments.description: Answers every channel with one brain and one calendar. The whole point is that nobody is promised a Thursday that is already gone.

departments.name: Sales & Quoting
departments.description: Builds and sends the quote, chases it, and then stops. The close is a person: it is the gate the whole quoting stage exists to reach.

departments.name: Operations & Delivery
departments.description: The messy stage. A signature makes the job, the scope makes the material list, and a no-show sub is reassigned off the bench file before the owner has looked at their phone. The field work itself stays a person and always will.

departments.name: Finance & Collections
departments.description: Not a department so much as what happens when a job ends. Closeout fires the invoice, Stripe collects, and an unpaid invoice writes its own reminder - which a person still approves before it sends.

departments.name: Integration Layer
departments.description: Not a stage - the substrate under all five. Claude Code reaches the CRM, the job system and the books over MCP; underneath that sit three plain files the owner edits directly: what things cost, what the rules are, and who is on the bench. No agent works from memory.

processes.name: Catch and qualify an inbound lead
processes.frequency: per inbound contact, about 120 a month
processes.description: Everything that rings, texts or messages arrives here and leaves either booked, referred out, or nudged. One agent brain across every channel, reading the real calendar.

kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Receive inbound call, text or DM
steps.notes:
Purpose: Catch every channel on the first ring so no lead waits for the owner to be free.
Inputs: Inbound call audio, SMS, web chat or social DM.
Procedure: Telephony or the message inbox hands the intake agent a transcript and the channel it came from; the agent opens or matches a CRM lead.
Output: An open lead record with the raw first contact attached.

steps.title: Screen for spam or robocall
steps.notes:
Purpose: Keep junk out of the pipeline and out of the lead count that marketing is judged on.
Inputs: The transcript and the caller's number.
Procedure: The agent checks the number against known-junk lists and the transcript against the spam patterns in rules.md.
Output: Either a live lead, or a closed one tagged spam.

steps.title: Capture name, address and job description
steps.notes:
Purpose: Get the four facts every later stage needs, while the client is still on the line.
Inputs: The live conversation.
Procedure: The agent asks for name, service address, what is wrong, and how urgent it is, and writes each to the lead record as it goes.
Output: A lead record with contact, address, described scope and urgency.

steps.title: Check job type and address against rules.md
steps.notes:
Purpose: Refuse work outside the service area or the trades taken, before a slot is offered for it.
Inputs: Service address, described job type, rules.md.
Procedure: The agent matches the address against the service area and the job type against the taken/refused lists.
Output: A decision to book or to refer out.

steps.title: Refer the lead to a partner shop
steps.notes:
Purpose: Turn work we cannot take into goodwill and a return referral, rather than a dead end.
Inputs: The lead record and the partner list in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent sends the client the partner's details and notifies the partner with the scope.
Output: A referred lead and a logged referral.

steps.title: Close the lead as out of area
steps.notes:
Purpose: End the branch explicitly so out-of-area volume is countable rather than invisible.
Inputs: The referred lead.
Procedure: The agent closes the lead with reason 'out of area' and the partner it went to.
Output: A closed lead that still counts in the demand figures.

steps.title: Read the calendar for genuinely open slots
steps.notes:
Purpose: Nobody gets promised a Thursday that is already gone. This is the whole reason intake reads the live calendar rather than a cached copy.
Inputs: The calendar, plus travel-time and job-duration rules.
Procedure: The integration pulls free/busy for the next 14 days and subtracts travel time around existing jobs.
Output: Two or three offerable windows that will still be free when the client says yes.

steps.title: Offer the caller two real appointment windows
steps.notes:
Purpose: Two options close better than an open question and cannot conflict with an existing job.
Inputs: The offerable windows.
Procedure: The agent offers two windows and takes the client's pick, or one alternative if neither works.
Output: A chosen window, or a client who wants to think about it.

steps.title: Confirm the booking and write it to the CRM
steps.notes:
Purpose: Make the booking real in the system of record at the moment the client agrees, not later.
Inputs: The chosen window and the lead record.
Procedure: The agent writes the appointment to the calendar and the CRM, and sends the client a confirmation.
Output: A booked appointment, or a lead marked for follow-up.

steps.title: Hand the booked job to quoting
steps.notes:
Purpose: Pass a complete scope forward so the quoting agent never re-interviews the client.
Inputs: The booked appointment and the captured scope.
Procedure: The agent writes a quoting task against the lead with scope, address, urgency and window.
Output: A quoting task ready to run.

steps.title: Lead booked and handed to quoting
steps.notes:
Purpose: Terminate the successful path where it actually ends: at the handoff, not at the phone call.
Inputs: The quoting task.
Procedure: The agent closes the intake run against the lead.
Output: An intake run closed as booked.

steps.title: Schedule a follow-up nudge for 48 hours
steps.notes:
Purpose: An undecided caller is not a lost one, and 48 hours is early enough to still be remembered.
Inputs: The lead record and the offered windows.
Procedure: The agent queues a follow-up message repeating the two windows, and holds no calendar slot for it.
Output: A queued nudge and a lead in pending state.

steps.title: Close the lead as pending follow-up
steps.notes:
Purpose: Name the undecided ending so it can be measured against the booked one.
Inputs: The pending lead.
Procedure: The agent closes the intake run with reason 'pending follow-up'.
Output: A pending lead that the nudge will reopen.

processes.name: Build, send and close a quote
processes.frequency: per booked lead, about 64 a month
processes.description: The agent prices the job off the pricing file, sends it, and chases it. Then it stops: the close is a person. Quotes above the auto-send limit in rules.md also wait for a human before they leave the building.

kpi.metric: Quote out within 4 hours of the site visit
kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Pull the job scope and site notes from the CRM
steps.notes:
Purpose: Start from what intake captured so the client is never asked the same question twice.
Inputs: The quoting task written by intake.
Procedure: The integration reads scope, address, urgency and any site photos into the quoting workspace.
Output: A scope packet ready to price.

steps.title: Draft the quote from pricing.yaml
steps.notes:
Purpose: Price from the one file the owner controls, so no price is ever invented by an agent.
Inputs: The scope packet and pricing.yaml.
Procedure: The agent maps each scope item to a priced line, applies the job-type multipliers in the file, and totals it.
Output: A draft quote with every line traceable to a pricing file entry.

steps.title: Is every line covered by pricing.yaml?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Catch the unpriced line here rather than letting an agent guess a number a client will hold us to.
Inputs: The draft quote.
Procedure: The agent lists any scope item with no matching entry in the pricing file.
Output: Either a fully priced quote, or a named gap for the owner.

steps.title: Price the uncovered line
steps.notes:
Purpose: Only the owner sets a price that does not exist yet. This is also how pricing.yaml grows.
Inputs: The named gap and the scope detail behind it.
Procedure: The owner gives a price and decides whether it is a one-off or belongs in pricing.yaml.
Output: A priced line, and often a new pricing file entry.

steps.title: Assemble the quote document
steps.notes:
Purpose: Produce the thing the client actually reads: scope, price, terms, and what is excluded.
Inputs: The fully priced quote and the terms in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent renders the quote with scope, line prices, payment terms and exclusions.
Output: A sendable quote document attached to the lead.

steps.title: Is the quote above the auto-send limit?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Small quotes should not wait on a human; large ones should. The limit is a number in rules.md, not a judgement call.
Inputs: The quote total and the auto-send limit in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent compares the total against the limit and routes accordingly.
Output: A quote either cleared to send or queued for the owner.

steps.title: Review and release the quote
steps.notes:
Purpose: A large number leaving the business gets one pair of human eyes. It is the cheapest gate in the business and catches the most.
Inputs: The assembled quote and the scope it came from.
Procedure: The owner reads the scope against the price and either releases it or says what to change.
Output: A released quote, or a revision note.

steps.title: Revise the quote against the owner's note
steps.notes:
Purpose: Turn the owner's correction into a corrected document without them editing it by hand.
Inputs: The revision note and the current quote.
Procedure: The agent applies the change, re-totals, and records what changed and why.
Output: A revised quote ready for another look.

steps.title: Go to: Review and release the quote
steps.notes:
Purpose: Send the revision back through the same gate rather than around it - a revised quote is still an unreviewed quote.
Inputs: The revised quote.
Procedure: Control returns to the review step.
Output: A second review pass.

steps.title: Send the quote and log it against the lead
steps.notes:
Purpose: Get the quote in front of the client in the channel they already used.
Inputs: The released quote.
Procedure: The agent sends it by the client's original channel and records the send time.
Output: A sent quote with a clock running on it.

steps.title: Chase the quote on day 2 and day 5
steps.notes:
Purpose: Most quotes die of silence. Two chases is the point where more starts costing goodwill.
Inputs: The sent quote and its age.
Procedure: The agent sends a short follow-up on day 2 and day 5 unless the client has replied.
Output: A reply, or a quote ready to be marked lost.

steps.title: Did the client accept?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Split the pipeline honestly so win rate is a measured number rather than a felt one.
Inputs: Client replies and quote age.
Procedure: The agent classifies the outcome and, when declined, asks once for the reason.
Output: A won or lost quote.

steps.title: Close the deal and confirm scope on a call
steps.notes:
Purpose: The close stays human. This is the gate that binds the business to do work at a price, and it is where the scope is confirmed out loud before anyone signs.
Inputs: The accepted quote and the client on the phone.
Procedure: The owner confirms scope, price, access and date, and answers whatever is actually blocking the yes.
Output: A confirmed deal ready for contract.

steps.title: Send the contract for e-signature
steps.notes:
Purpose: Paper follows the human close, never precedes it. The agent may send the contract only because a person has just closed the deal.
Inputs: The confirmed deal.
Procedure: The agent fills the contract from the quote and sends it for signature.
Output: A contract out for signature.

steps.title: Job won and awaiting signature
steps.notes:
Purpose: End the won path at the contract, because the signature is what starts operations.
Inputs: The sent contract.
Procedure: The agent marks the quote won and hands the lead to the signature webhook.
Output: A won quote awaiting a signature event.

steps.title: Log the loss reason against the quote
steps.notes:
Purpose: A loss without a reason teaches nothing. The repricing loop reads these.
Inputs: The decline and any stated reason.
Procedure: The agent records price, timing, scope or competitor against the quote.
Output: A lost quote with a reason attached.

steps.title: Quote lost
steps.notes:
Purpose: Name the losing ending so win rate has a denominator.
Inputs: The lost quote.
Procedure: The agent closes the quoting run.
Output: A closed, lost quote.

processes.name: Run a booked job to closeout
processes.frequency: per signed contract, about 38 a month
processes.description: The signature makes the job, the scope makes the material list, and a sub who does not show is replaced off bench.csv with the client told before the owner has looked at their phone. Supplier orders above the spend limit wait for a person. The work itself is four hours of one and no agent changes that.

kpi.metric: Jobs invoiced within 24 hours of closeout
kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Receive the signed contract
steps.notes:
Purpose: Make the signature - not a human noticing the signature - the thing that starts operations.
Inputs: The signature event from the e-signature service.
Procedure: The webhook fires into the job system with the contract and its quote.
Output: A signature event carrying the agreed scope.

steps.title: Create the job and hold the calendar slot
steps.notes:
Purpose: Turn the agreement into a scheduled job in one write, so nothing sits in an inbox waiting to be typed up.
Inputs: The signature event and the window agreed at close.
Procedure: The integration creates the job, attaches the scope, and converts the held window into a booked calendar entry.
Output: A scheduled job with the scope attached.

steps.title: Build the material list from the scope
steps.notes:
Purpose: The scope already says what the job needs; retyping it into a shopping list is exactly the work an agent should absorb.
Inputs: The job scope and the material rules in pricing.yaml.
Procedure: The agent expands each scope line into quantities and parts, and flags anything with a lead time.
Output: A material list with lead-time items marked.

steps.title: Is everything on the material list in stock?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Find the missing part now rather than on the morning of the job.
Inputs: The material list and current stock.
Procedure: The agent checks each line against stock and lead time against the job date.
Output: Either a job that can proceed, or a supplier order to place.

steps.title: Is the order above the spend limit?
steps.notes:
Purpose: A small parts order should not wait on a human; a large one should. Same shape as the quote auto-send limit, and the same reason: the threshold is a number in rules.md, so the routing is arithmetic rather than an agent's judgement about how much money is a lot.
Inputs: The order total and the supplier spend limit in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent totals the order and compares it against the limit.
Output: An order either cleared to place or queued for the owner.

steps.title: Approve the supplier order
steps.notes:
Purpose: Money leaving the business for a large parts order gets a person, even though the client has already signed for the job. An approval that cannot refuse is not an approval, so this one forks.
Inputs: The order, the job it is for, and the quoted material allowance.
Procedure: The owner checks the order against what was quoted, and either releases it or takes the sourcing over - trade counter, an offcut in the van, a supplier the file does not know about.
Output: Either a released order, or one the owner has taken off the agent.

steps.title: Place the supplier order
steps.notes:
Purpose: Order against the job so the cost lands on the job and shows up in repricing later.
Inputs: The cleared order and the supplier list.
Procedure: The agent places the order coded to the job number and records the promised date.
Output: An ordered part with a delivery date against the job.

steps.title: Assign a crew or sub from bench.csv
steps.notes:
Purpose: Assignment is a lookup, not a decision: the bench file is already in preference order.
Inputs: The job trade and date, and bench.csv.
Procedure: The agent picks the first available name whose trade matches, and sends them the job pack.
Output: An assigned sub who has the scope and the address.

steps.title: Did the sub confirm 24 hours out?
steps.notes:
Purpose: The no-show is the single most expensive event in the week. Catching it a day early is what makes it recoverable.
Inputs: The assignment and the sub's reply.
Procedure: The agent requests confirmation 24 hours before and treats silence as a decline.
Output: A confirmed sub, or a hole to fill.

steps.title: Pull the next name off the bench and reassign
steps.notes:
Purpose: Recover the slot from the file rather than from the owner's memory of who owes them a favour.
Inputs: bench.csv and the unfilled job.
Procedure: The agent walks the bench in order until one accepts, and records who declined.
Output: A reassigned job, or an escalation if the bench is exhausted.

steps.title: Text the client the new crew and window
steps.notes:
Purpose: The client hears about the change from us before they notice it themselves. This is the beat that decides whether a no-show costs a review.
Inputs: The reassignment.
Procedure: The agent texts the client the new name and confirms the window is unchanged.
Output: A client informed before they had to ask.

steps.title: Wait for the scheduled job date
steps.notes:
Purpose: The gap between booking and doing is real elapsed time and belongs on the map; leaving it as white space hides where the cash is.
Inputs: The booked date.
Procedure: Nothing runs. The job sits scheduled.
Output: The job date arrives.

steps.title: Do the job on site
steps.notes:
Purpose: The work. No agent does this, and the architecture is honest only if the map says so.
Inputs: The material list, the access details and the scope.
Procedure: The owner or the assigned sub does the job.
Output: A completed job.

steps.title: Capture closeout photos and the final scope
steps.notes:
Purpose: The closeout pack is what the invoice is built from, so it is captured on site while the evidence still exists.
Inputs: The finished work.
Procedure: The owner photographs the work, notes anything done differently, and gets the client's sign-off in the job app.
Output: A closeout pack: photos, final scope, client signature.

steps.title: Did the scope change on site?
steps.notes:
Purpose: An unbilled change order is a straight loss, and it is the most common one in this trade.
Inputs: The final scope against the quoted scope.
Procedure: The agent diffs the two and flags any added or removed line.
Output: Either a matching job, or a priced change to agree.

steps.title: Price the change order and get the client's OK
steps.notes:
Purpose: Charging a client more than they agreed to is a human conversation, on site, before they leave.
Inputs: The flagged scope difference and pricing.yaml.
Procedure: The owner prices the change, explains it, and takes the client's agreement in writing in the job app.
Output: An agreed change order attached to the job.

steps.title: Is the closeout pack complete?
steps.notes:
Purpose: An invoice built from a half-finished pack is the invoice that gets disputed at day 40.
Inputs: The closeout pack and the job's requirements.
Procedure: The agent checks photos, final scope, signature and any change order are all present.
Output: Either a complete pack, or a named missing item.

steps.title: Ask the owner for the missing item
steps.notes:
Purpose: Ask while the owner can still walk back to the site, not at the end of the month.
Inputs: The named missing item.
Procedure: The agent texts the owner exactly what is missing and holds the invoice.
Output: The missing item supplied.

steps.title: Go to: Is the closeout pack complete?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Re-run the check rather than trusting that the gap was filled correctly.
Inputs: The supplied item.
Procedure: Control returns to the completeness check.
Output: A second completeness pass.

steps.title: Issue the invoice from the closeout pack
steps.notes:
Purpose: Nobody types an invoice. The closeout is the trigger, and the pack is the source, so the invoice cannot disagree with the job.
Inputs: The complete closeout pack and any change order.
Procedure: The integration builds the invoice from quoted lines plus agreed changes and issues it with a payment link.
Output: An issued invoice with a Stripe payment link.

steps.title: Order held for the owner to source
steps.notes:
Purpose: Name the ending where the owner takes the buying back, so it is countable rather than looking like an order that never happened.
Inputs: The owner's decision to source it themselves.
Procedure: The agent closes the order line against the job and notes that the owner is sourcing.
Output: A job whose parts the owner is handling.

steps.title: Job closed and invoiced
steps.notes:
Purpose: End operations at the invoice, which is where finance picks the job up.
Inputs: The issued invoice.
Procedure: The job is marked complete and handed to collections.
Output: A closed job and an open invoice.

processes.name: Collect on an issued invoice
processes.description: Stripe collects. When it does not, the agent writes the awkward message for the owner - and then waits for them to approve it, because a demand is a relationship decision, not a template.

kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Issue the invoice and payment link
steps.notes:
Purpose: Give the client a way to pay in the same moment they are told what they owe.
Inputs: The closeout pack.
Procedure: The integration issues the invoice through Stripe and emails and texts the link.
Output: An open invoice with a live payment link.

steps.title: Wait out the payment terms
steps.notes:
Purpose: The terms in rules.md are a real wait and the largest single component of days-sales-outstanding.
Inputs: The invoice date and the terms.
Procedure: Nothing runs. The invoice sits inside terms.
Output: Terms expire.

steps.title: Has the invoice been paid?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Stripe is the only authority on payment. Nothing else is allowed to mark an invoice paid.
Inputs: Stripe's payment record.
Procedure: The integration checks the invoice status the day terms expire.
Output: A paid or unpaid invoice.

steps.title: Send the day-7 payment nudge
steps.notes:
Purpose: Most late invoices are forgotten, not refused, and a friendly nudge recovers them without costing anything.
Inputs: The overdue invoice and the client's history.
Procedure: The agent sends a short, warm reminder with the payment link.
Output: A nudged client.

steps.title: Wait for the nudge to land
steps.notes:
Purpose: A week is long enough for a genuine payment run and short enough to still be inside the relationship.
Inputs: The nudge date.
Procedure: Nothing runs.
Output: Seven days pass.

steps.title: Has the nudge been paid?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Second checkpoint, and the one that decides whether this becomes a demand.
Inputs: Stripe's payment record.
Procedure: The integration re-checks the invoice status.
Output: A paid invoice, or one heading for a demand.

steps.title: Draft the day-30 demand and hold it
steps.notes:
Purpose: Write the awkward message so the owner does not have to - but hold it, because sending it is their call.
Inputs: The invoice, the nudge history and the client's whole history.
Procedure: The agent drafts a firm, specific message naming the amount, the age and the next step, and queues it unsent.
Output: A drafted demand awaiting approval.

steps.title: Approve the demand before it sends
steps.notes:
Purpose: A demand can end a client relationship. The agent may write it; only the owner may send it.
Inputs: The drafted demand and what the owner knows about the client.
Procedure: The owner reads it and either releases it or decides to handle it personally.
Output: A released demand, or a call to make.

steps.title: Send the demand and log the escalation date
steps.notes:
Purpose: Send what the owner approved, unchanged, and set the clock for the next decision.
Inputs: The approved demand.
Procedure: The agent sends it and records an escalation date 14 days out.
Output: A sent demand with an escalation date.

steps.title: Go to: Has the nudge been paid?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Return to the payment check rather than drawing a fourth escalation branch: the question is the same one.
Inputs: The escalation date.
Procedure: Control returns to the payment check.
Output: Another payment check at the escalation date.

steps.title: Call the client and settle it
steps.notes:
Purpose: Some debts are a conversation. The owner takes the ones where the relationship is worth more than the invoice.
Inputs: The invoice and its history.
Procedure: The owner calls, agrees a payment or a write-off, and records which.
Output: A settled or written-off debt.

steps.title: Debt settled or written off by the owner
steps.notes:
Purpose: End the human branch explicitly so write-offs are countable against the repricing loop.
Inputs: The owner's decision.
Procedure: The outcome is written to the books against the job.
Output: A closed invoice with a named outcome.

steps.title: Reconcile the payment into the books
steps.notes:
Purpose: Get the cash against the job, because the repricing and ad-budget loops both read actual cash, not invoiced amounts.
Inputs: The Stripe payment.
Procedure: The integration matches the payment to the invoice and the invoice to the job, and posts it.
Output: A reconciled payment attached to its job.

steps.title: Invoice closed
steps.notes:
Purpose: Close the loop's money leg where the cash actually lands.
Inputs: The reconciled payment.
Procedure: The invoice is closed and the job's real margin becomes computable.
Output: A closed invoice feeding the repricing loop.

processes.name: Reconcile quoted against actual and reprice
processes.description: Checks what was quoted against what the job actually cost, and moves a price only when the evidence clears two gates: enough jobs of that type, and a drift interval that excludes zero. Below either gate it reports the shortfall and leaves the price alone, because a one-van shop does not generate enough jobs a month to reprice off noise.

kpi.metric: Job types with a margin estimate that clears the sample gate
kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Pull closed jobs with quoted and actual cost
steps.notes:
Purpose: Read actual cost from the reconciled ledger, never from an estimate or a memory of the job.
Inputs: Closed jobs and their posted costs.
Procedure: The integration exports each closed job's type, quoted price, actual material and labour cost, and change orders.
Output: A table of closed jobs with real margins.

steps.title: Group by job type and compute margin drift
steps.notes:
Purpose: Compare like with like: a bathroom and a callout have nothing to say about each other's pricing.
Inputs: The closed-job table.
Procedure: The agent groups by job type and computes mean margin, its spread, and drift against the price in pricing.yaml.
Output: Per-type margin drift with a job count and an interval.

steps.title: Does any job type clear the sample-size gate?
steps.notes:
Purpose: The gate exists because this business does 38 jobs a month across several types. Most months, most types have too few jobs to say anything.
Inputs: Per-type job counts and the floor in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent compares each type's count against the floor and drops the types below it.
Output: Either types with enough evidence, or a report that there are none.

steps.title: Report the shortfall and leave prices alone
steps.notes:
Purpose: Saying 'not enough jobs yet' is the correct output most months, and it has to be a visible ending rather than silence.
Inputs: The per-type counts.
Procedure: The agent reports how many more jobs each type needs before it can be repriced.
Output: A no-change report naming what is still missing.

steps.title: Does the drift interval exclude zero?
steps.notes:
Purpose: Enough jobs is not the same as a real signal. A drift whose interval straddles zero is noise with a mean attached.
Inputs: The margin drift and its interval for each qualifying type.
Procedure: The agent keeps only the types whose interval sits entirely above or below zero.
Output: Either proven drift, or a report that the drift is unproven.

steps.title: Report the drift as unproven and leave prices alone
steps.notes:
Purpose: The second no-change ending. It looks like the first and is a different fact, so it is named separately.
Inputs: The intervals that straddle zero.
Procedure: The agent reports the observed drift and why it does not justify a change.
Output: A no-change report naming the drift and its uncertainty.

steps.title: Draft the price change with its evidence
steps.notes:
Purpose: A price change arrives with the jobs behind it attached, so the owner is approving evidence rather than a suggestion.
Inputs: The proven drift and the affected pricing.yaml lines.
Procedure: The agent drafts the new price, the job count, the drift and interval, and the effect on the last ten quotes.
Output: A proposed price change with its evidence.

steps.title: Approve or reject the price change
steps.notes:
Purpose: Prices are how the business competes. An agent that can move them can lose every bid without anyone noticing until the calendar empties.
Inputs: The proposal and the owner's read of the local market.
Procedure: The owner accepts, rejects, or accepts a smaller move.
Output: An approved or rejected price change.

steps.title: Write the new price into pricing.yaml
steps.notes:
Purpose: The owner's hand on the pricing file is the point. Agents read it; only a person writes it.
Inputs: The approved change.
Procedure: The owner edits pricing.yaml and commits it with the reason.
Output: An updated pricing file with a change reason in its history.

steps.title: Pricing updated
steps.notes:
Purpose: End the approved path at the file, because the file is what every future quote reads.
Inputs: The updated pricing file.
Procedure: The next quote prices off the new number.
Output: New prices live.

steps.title: Log the rejection and the reason
steps.notes:
Purpose: A rejected proposal is evidence about the owner's judgement and should not be proposed again identically next month.
Inputs: The rejection and the owner's reason.
Procedure: The agent records the proposal, the rejection and the reason against the job type.
Output: A logged rejection the next run will read.

steps.title: Price left unchanged
steps.notes:
Purpose: Name the rejected ending so proposal-acceptance rate is measurable.
Inputs: The logged rejection.
Procedure: The run closes with no price change.
Output: Prices unchanged.

processes.name: Set next week's ad budget from collected cash
processes.description: The step that makes this a loop instead of a funnel. Last week's collected cash and job margin decide this week's ad spend, the owner approves the number, and the agent applies the number the owner approved.

kpi.current: unmeasured until the business is instrumented

steps.title: Pull last week's collected cash and job margin
steps.notes:
Purpose: Budget off cash that actually landed, not invoices that might. This is the difference between a loop and a wish.
Inputs: The reconciled ledger for the week.
Procedure: The integration totals collected cash and per-job margin for jobs closed in the week.
Output: A week of real cash and margin.

steps.title: Pull spend, leads and cost per lead by channel
steps.notes:
Purpose: Attribute demand to the channel that produced it, so the budget can move rather than just grow.
Inputs: Ad platform reporting and CRM lead sources.
Procedure: The integration pulls spend and leads per channel and joins them to booked jobs in the CRM.
Output: Cost per lead and cost per booked job, by channel.

steps.title: Compute contribution per job and CAC payback
steps.notes:
Purpose: One number decides the week: does a job pay back what it cost to win it, and how fast.
Inputs: Weekly cash, margin, and per-channel acquisition cost.
Procedure: The agent computes contribution per job, blended CAC, and payback in jobs and days.
Output: A payback figure to test against the rule.

steps.title: Does the loop clear its payback rule?
steps.notes:
Purpose: The rule is a number in rules.md so the answer is arithmetic rather than optimism.
Inputs: The payback figure and the rule in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent compares payback against the ceiling in the rules file.
Output: A verdict to raise or to cut.

steps.title: Draft a budget raise capped by the weekly ceiling
steps.notes:
Purpose: A working loop should be fed, but never faster than the calendar can absorb - the ceiling is capacity, not confidence.
Inputs: The payback figure, current spend, and the weekly ceiling in rules.md.
Procedure: The agent proposes a raise on the best-payback channel, capped by the ceiling and by open calendar capacity.
Output: A proposed budget raise.

steps.title: Go to: Approve the ad budget
steps.notes:
Purpose: Both drafts meet at the same approval rather than each having its own, so there is exactly one place money gets released.
Inputs: The proposed raise.
Procedure: Control jumps to the approval step.
Output: One shared approval.

steps.title: Draft a budget cut on the worst channel
steps.notes:
Purpose: A loop that does not pay back gets smaller. Cutting the worst channel first is what keeps the good one funded.
Inputs: Per-channel payback and current spend.
Procedure: The agent proposes a cut on the worst-payback channel and leaves the rest untouched.
Output: A proposed budget cut.

steps.title: Approve the ad budget
steps.notes:
Purpose: Ad spend is the only button in this business that spends money continuously without anyone doing any work. That is what puts a person in front of it.
Inputs: The proposed budget change and its evidence.
Procedure: The owner approves, rejects, or sets a different number.
Output: An approved budget figure, or a rejection.

steps.title: Apply the approved budget on the ad platforms
steps.notes:
Purpose: The agent sets the number a person just approved. It has no discretion here - the human decided the amount, the agent only types it into four platforms so the owner does not have to.
Inputs: The approved figure.
Procedure: The agent writes the budget to each platform and reads it back to confirm it took.
Output: A live budget matching the approved figure.

steps.title: Budget set for the week
steps.notes:
Purpose: End the loop where it restarts: the money that finance collected is now buying the phone calls intake will answer.
Inputs: The live budget.
Procedure: The week runs and produces the leads the loop starts on.
Output: A funded week of demand.

steps.title: Log the rejection and hold last week's budget
steps.notes:
Purpose: Rejection means no change, not zero. Holding is a decision and is recorded as one.
Inputs: The rejection.
Procedure: The agent records the rejection and leaves the existing budget in place.
Output: An unchanged budget and a logged rejection.

steps.title: Budget unchanged
steps.notes:
Purpose: Name the held ending so 'we did nothing' is visible in the weekly record.
Inputs: The logged rejection.
Procedure: The week runs on last week's budget.
Output: An unchanged week.

tools.name: Voice line & IVR
tools.purpose: Answers the phone, transcribes the caller, hands the text to the intake agent.

tools.name: SMS & DM inbox
tools.purpose: One thread per client across text, web chat and social DMs, so every channel reaches the same agent.

tools.name: CRM
tools.purpose: System of record for leads, quotes and clients. Every agent reads and writes here rather than holding state.

tools.name: Calendar
tools.purpose: The single source of what is actually free. Agents read it before offering a slot; they never quote availability from memory.

tools.name: Field job system
tools.purpose: Jobs, scopes, material lists, crew assignment and the closeout pack.

tools.name: E-signature
tools.purpose: Sends the contract and fires a webhook on signature, which is what creates the job.

tools.name: Stripe
tools.purpose: Issues the payment link, collects, and is the only authority on whether an invoice is paid.

tools.name: Accounting (QuickBooks or similar)
tools.purpose: Reconciled ledger. The repricing loop reads actual cost from here, never from an estimate.

tools.name: Ad platforms
tools.purpose: Local service ads and paid search. The only place the business can spend money at the push of a button.

tools.name: Claude Code over MCP
tools.purpose: The one layer on top. Every agent reaches every system through it, so there is a single place where permissions and logging live.

tools.name: pricing.yaml
tools.purpose: What every line item costs. The quoting agent may read it; only the owner writes it.

tools.name: rules.md
tools.purpose: Service area, job types taken and refused, auto-send limit, payment terms, escalation thresholds. Written once, read by every agent.

tools.name: bench.csv
tools.purpose: Subs and crews in preference order, with trades and rates. This file is what makes a no-show recoverable in minutes.

changes.title: Placed the close at the human gate, not the send
changes.description: The quoting agent builds, sends and chases, then stops. A person confirms scope and closes on a call before any contract goes out. The agent is allowed to send the contract only because a person closed the deal in the step immediately before it.
changes.author: Owner-operator

changes.title: Added an auto-send limit rather than reviewing every quote
changes.description: Reviewing all 64 quotes a month costs more attention than it saves. Quotes under the limit in rules.md go straight out; quotes over it wait for the owner. The limit is a number in a file, so the routing is arithmetic instead of a judgement call the agent has to make.
changes.author: Owner-operator

changes.title: Gated repricing on sample size before drift
changes.description: At 38 jobs a month across several job types, most types have too few jobs in a month to distinguish a margin drift from noise. Repricing now reports 'not enough jobs yet' as a first-class outcome and only proposes a change when the count clears the floor and the drift interval excludes zero.
changes.author: Owner-operator

roadmap.title: After-hours voice intake
roadmap.description: Own the 6pm-8am calls with a different script and a next-morning callback promise. Splits out of the Intake agent; justified when after-hours volume passes 20 calls a month.

roadmap.title: Daytime overflow voice intake
roadmap.description: Pick up calls that arrive while another is live, instead of queueing them. Splits out of the Intake agent; justified when simultaneous-call rate passes 5% of volume.

roadmap.title: SMS and text intake
roadmap.description: Split texting off voice so tone and pacing can differ from a phone script. Splits out of the Intake agent; justified when text is over a third of inbound.

roadmap.title: Web chat intake
roadmap.description: Handle site visitors, who arrive with less context and need more qualifying. Splits out of the Intake agent; justified when the site produces 15+ chats a month.

roadmap.title: Social DM intake
roadmap.description: Instagram and Facebook messages, where identity and address are hardest to pin down. Splits out of the Intake agent; justified when social produces 10+ leads a month.

roadmap.title: Service-type classifier
roadmap.description: Map a described problem to a job type, which everything downstream keys off. Splits out of the Qualifier agent; justified when job types pass 12.

roadmap.title: Service-area checker
roadmap.description: Address-level geo and travel-time checks rather than a postcode list. Splits out of the Qualifier agent; justified when edge-of-area jobs start losing money on travel.

roadmap.title: Urgency triage
roadmap.description: Separate emergency from scheduled work and price the difference. Splits out of the Qualifier agent; justified when emergency work passes 15% of jobs.

roadmap.title: Budget probe
roadmap.description: Find the client's ceiling before a quote is built for a job they will never buy. Splits out of the Qualifier agent; justified when quote-to-win rate falls under 40%.

roadmap.title: Spam and robocall filter
roadmap.description: A dedicated screen once junk volume makes the intake agent's transcript costs material. Splits out of the Qualifier agent; justified when junk passes 25% of inbound.

roadmap.title: Scope extractor
roadmap.description: Turn a rambling description and site photos into structured scope lines. Splits out of the Quoting agent; justified when scope errors cause 3+ change orders a month.

roadmap.title: Material take-off
roadmap.description: Expand scope into quantities and parts, which is a different skill from pricing them. Splits out of the Quoting agent; justified when material cost passes 40% of job cost.

roadmap.title: Labour estimator
roadmap.description: Estimate hours per job type from the closed-job record instead of a flat rate. Splits out of the Quoting agent; justified when labour variance passes 25% of estimate.

roadmap.title: Quote follow-up chaser
roadmap.description: Own the day-2 and day-5 chase and learn what wording gets replies. Splits out of the Quoting agent; justified when open quotes pass 30 at a time.

roadmap.title: Upsell and bundle suggester
roadmap.description: Propose the adjacent job while the crew is already on site. Splits out of the Quoting agent; justified when repeat-visit rate suggests bundling would land.

roadmap.title: Crew assignment
roadmap.description: Match trade, rating and history to the job rather than walking the bench in order. Splits out of the Dispatch agent; justified when the bench passes 10 names.

roadmap.title: Bench fallback
roadmap.description: Own the no-show recovery path, which is time-critical and needs its own escalation ladder. Splits out of the Dispatch agent; justified when no-shows pass 4 a month.

roadmap.title: Route and travel-time optimiser
roadmap.description: Sequence the day's jobs so travel is not silently eating the margin. Splits out of the Dispatch agent; justified when jobs per day passes 3.

roadmap.title: Client ETA notifier
roadmap.description: Live arrival windows, which is the single most-asked question in this trade. Splits out of the Dispatch agent; justified when 'where are they' calls pass 10 a month.

roadmap.title: Weather and permit watcher
roadmap.description: Catch the rained-off or unpermitted job before the crew is dispatched to it. Splits out of the Dispatch agent; justified when weather-cancelled jobs pass 2 a month.

roadmap.title: Pre-job checklist
roadmap.description: Confirm access, parking, pets and power before the van leaves. Splits out of the Closeout agent; justified when aborted visits pass 2 a month.

roadmap.title: Photo quality control
roadmap.description: Reject a closeout pack whose photos will not survive a dispute. Splits out of the Closeout agent; justified when disputes pass 1 a month.

roadmap.title: Change-order catcher
roadmap.description: Own the scope diff and the on-site conversation prompt. Splits out of the Closeout agent; justified when unbilled changes pass $500 a month.

roadmap.title: Warranty and callback logger
roadmap.description: Track callbacks against the original job so repeat failures surface. Splits out of the Closeout agent; justified when callbacks pass 3 a month.

roadmap.title: Payment reconciler
roadmap.description: Match payments to invoices to jobs when partials and deposits make it non-obvious. Splits out of the Collections agent; justified when partial payments pass 10% of invoices.

roadmap.title: Day-7 nudge writer
roadmap.description: Own the warm reminder, tuned per client history. Splits out of the Collections agent; justified when overdue invoices pass 10 a month.

roadmap.title: Day-30 demand writer
roadmap.description: Own the firm message, which is a different register and higher stakes. Splits out of the Collections agent; justified when 30-day invoices pass 5 a month.

roadmap.title: Deposit and retainer tracker
roadmap.description: Track money taken before work, which ages differently from an invoice. Splits out of the Collections agent; justified when deposits are taken on more than a quarter of jobs.

roadmap.title: Statement and receipt sender
roadmap.description: Month-end statements for commercial clients who pay off statements, not invoices. Splits out of the Collections agent; justified when commercial clients pass 5.

roadmap.title: Win-rate analyst
roadmap.description: Separate lost-on-price from lost-on-timing, which the single agent conflates. Splits out of the Pricing analyst agent; justified when quote volume passes 100 a month.

roadmap.title: Ad-channel allocator
roadmap.description: Per-channel budget moves rather than one blended raise or cut. Splits out of the Pricing analyst agent; justified when channels pass 3.

roadmap.title: Review requester
roadmap.description: Ask for the review at the moment the job lands well, which is a narrow window. Splits out of the Pricing analyst agent; justified when review volume matters to local ranking.

roadmap.title: Dormant-client reactivation
roadmap.description: Work the back catalogue, which nothing else in the loop touches. Splits out of the Pricing analyst agent; justified when the client list passes 300.

roadmap.title: Instrument every KPI on this map
roadmap.description: Every process here carries a target and a 'current' of 'unmeasured'. Until the real business is instrumented, none of the before/after claims this architecture makes can be checked.

roadmap.title: Map the current process before adopting this as a target
roadmap.description: This is a target design with no baseline behind it. The hours-returned figure is undefined until someone maps how the business runs today and prices its person steps. Phase 2 of the readiness framework is that map.
